lines.text: Snap a stick in two random places, and you get three pieces.
lines.caption: Snap a stick in 2 random places, and you get 3 pieces.

lines.text: Is the longest piece less than twice the shortest? Here's a hint: it's rarer than you might think.
lines.caption: Is the longest piece less than twice the shortest? Here's a hint: it's rarer than you might think.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's turn this stick puzzle into a picture.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's turn this stick puzzle into a picture.

lines.text: Here's the question: a stick is cut at two points, chosen at random along its length. That makes three pieces.
lines.caption: Here's the question: a stick is cut at 2 points, chosen at random along its length. That makes 3 pieces.

lines.text: What is the probability that the longest piece is less than twice as long as the shortest piece?
lines.caption: What is the probability that the longest piece is less than twice as long as the shortest piece?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the 5 choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Let's make the stick sixty units long. Any length gives the same chance.
lines.caption: Let's make the stick 60 units long. Any length gives the same chance.

lines.text: Pieces of sixteen, twenty and twenty-four win. Twenty-four is less than two times sixteen, thirty-two.
lines.caption: Pieces of 16, 20 and 24 win. 24 is less than 2 times 16, 32.

lines.text: But ten, twenty and thirty loses. Thirty is NOT less than two times ten, which is twenty.
lines.caption: But 10, 20 and 30 loses. 30 is NOT less than 2 times 10, which is 20.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Call the first cut x and the second y: every pair of cuts is a dot in a sixty by sixty square.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Call the first cut x and the second y: every pair of cuts is a dot in a 60 by 60 square.

lines.text: Random cuts give a random dot. So the chance is a share of the square's area, three thousand six hundred.
lines.caption: Random cuts give a random dot. So the chance is a share of the square's area, 3600.

lines.text: Above the diagonal, the second cut is further right. The pieces are x, y minus x, and sixty minus y.
lines.caption: Above the diagonal, the second cut is further right. The pieces are x, y minus x, and 60 minus y.

lines.text: Below the diagonal is a mirror copy. So let's work in the top half. Its area is one thousand eight hundred.
lines.caption: Below the diagonal is a mirror copy. So let's work in the top half. Its area is 1800.

lines.text: Which piece is shortest? Three lines, where two pieces are equal, cut the top half into six slices.
lines.caption: Which piece is shortest? 3 lines, where 2 pieces are equal, cut the top half into 6 slices.

lines.text: All three lines meet at one point, where every piece is twenty.
lines.caption: All 3 lines meet at one point, where every piece is 20.

lines.text: Take the slice where left is shortest and right is longest. Its base is thirty, and its height is twenty.
lines.caption: Take the slice where left is shortest and right is longest. Its base is 30, and its height is 20.

lines.text: So its area is half of thirty times twenty. That's three hundred.
lines.caption: So its area is half of 30 times 20. That's 300.

lines.text: No piece is special, so all six slices have the same area. Six times three hundred is one thousand eight hundred!
lines.caption: No piece is special, so all 6 slices have the same area. 6 times 300 is 1800!

lines.text: In our slice, we win when the right piece is less than two times the left piece.
lines.caption: In our slice, we win when the right piece is less than 2 times the left piece.

lines.text: Where left equals middle, the border has right equal to two lefts. That's one, one, two parts of sixty: fifteen, fifteen, thirty.
lines.caption: Where left equals middle, the border has right equal to 2 lefts. That's 1, 1, 2 parts of 60: 15, 15, 30.

lines.text: Where middle equals right, right is still two lefts. That's one, two, two parts of sixty: twelve, twenty-four, twenty-four.
lines.caption: Where middle equals right, right is still 2 lefts. That's 1, 2, 2 parts of 60: 12, 24, 24.

lines.text: So the winning part is a small triangle, from the equal point to these two spots.
lines.caption: So the winning part is a small triangle, from the equal point to these 2 spots.

lines.text: Let's find its area with a box trick. The box is eight wide and ten tall, so its area is eighty.
lines.caption: Let's find its area with a box trick. The box is 8 wide and 10 tall, so its area is 80.

lines.text: Cut off the three right triangles around ours. Half of five times ten is twenty-five.
lines.caption: Cut off the 3 right triangles around ours. Half of 5 times 10 is 25.

lines.text: Half of four times eight is sixteen. Half of three times six is nine.
lines.caption: Half of 4 times 8 is 16. Half of 3 times 6 is 9.

lines.text: That's fifty in all. So the winning triangle is eighty minus fifty. That's thirty!
lines.caption: That's 50 in all. So the winning triangle is 80 minus 50. That's 30!

lines.text: Every slice works the same way. Six winning triangles make a hexagon of one hundred eighty.
lines.caption: Every slice works the same way. 6 winning triangles make a hexagon of 180.

lines.text: The bottom half is a mirror copy. So the chance is one hundred eighty out of one thousand eight hundred.
lines.caption: The bottom half is a mirror copy. So the chance is 180 out of 1800.

lines.text: That's <short pause> one over ten! Choice C.
lines.caption: That's 1/10! Choice C.

lines.text: Here's a faster way, with no box at all. Stay in our slice, and start at the equal point.
lines.caption: Here's a faster way, with no box at all. Stay in our slice, and start at the equal point.

lines.text: Walk along an edge to the far corner. The shortest piece shrinks steadily, from twenty down to zero.
lines.caption: Walk along an edge to the far corner. The shortest piece shrinks steadily, from 20 down to 0.

lines.text: On edge one, we already found the border: fifteen, fifteen, thirty.
lines.caption: On edge one, we already found the border: 15, 15, 30.

lines.text: The shortest piece shrank five out of twenty. That's one over four of the way.
lines.caption: The shortest piece shrank 5 out of 20. That's 1/4 of the way.

lines.text: On edge two, we already found the border: twelve, twenty-four, twenty-four.
lines.caption: On edge 2, we already found the border: 12, 24, 24.

lines.text: It shrank eight out of twenty. That's two over five of the way.
lines.caption: It shrank 8 out of 20. That's 2/5 of the way.

lines.text: Shrink two sides of a triangle toward one corner, and its area shrinks by both fractions, multiplied.
lines.caption: Shrink 2 sides of a triangle toward one corner, and its area shrinks by both fractions, multiplied.

lines.text: One over four, times two over five, is one over ten. Much faster! Pick this when the winning part sits in a corner.
lines.caption: 1/4, times 2/5, is 1/10. Much faster! Pick this when the winning part sits in a corner.

lines.text: Now, the traps.
lines.caption: Now, the traps.

lines.text: A, one over twenty, is what you'd get if you forgot the mirror copy below the diagonal.
lines.caption: A, 1/20, is what you'd get if you forgot the mirror copy below the diagonal.

lines.text: B, one over twelve, is what you'd get if one whole slice counted as a win.
lines.caption: B, 1/12, is what you'd get if one whole slice counted as a win.

lines.text: D, one over six, is the chance of just one ordering. It forgets the twice-as-long rule.
lines.caption: D, 1/6, is the chance of just one ordering. It forgets the twice-as-long rule.

lines.text: Choice E, one over four, is the famous chance that the three pieces can make a triangle. Our test is stricter!
lines.caption: Choice E, 1/4, is the famous chance that the 3 pieces can make a triangle. Our test is stricter!

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same stick, but an easier test.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same stick, but an easier test.

lines.text: What's the chance that the longest piece is less than THREE times the shortest?
lines.caption: What's the chance that the longest piece is less than 3 times the shortest?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's walk again, with a stick one hundred five long.
lines.caption: Let's walk again, with a stick 105 long.

lines.text: The equal point has three pieces of thirty-five. On edge one, ratio one, one, three gives twenty-one, twenty-one, sixty-three.
lines.caption: The equal point has 3 pieces of 35. On edge 1, ratio 1, 1, 3 gives 21, 21, 63.

lines.text: The shortest piece shrank fourteen out of thirty-five. That's two over five of the way.
lines.caption: The shortest piece shrank 14 out of 35. That's 2/5 of the way.

lines.text: On edge two, ratio one, three, three gives fifteen, forty-five, forty-five.
lines.caption: On edge 2, ratio 1, 3, 3 gives 15, 45, 45.

lines.text: It shrank twenty out of thirty-five. That's four over seven of the way.
lines.caption: It shrank 20 out of 35. That's 4/7 of the way.

lines.text: Two over five, times four over seven, is <short pause> eight over thirty-five!
lines.caption: 2/5, times 4/7, is 8/35!

lines.text: The big idea: two random cuts make a random dot in a square.
lines.caption: The big idea: 2 random cuts make a random dot in a square.

lines.text: Every ordering of the pieces gets an equal slice. So find the winning share of just one slice.
lines.caption: Every ordering of the pieces gets an equal slice. So find the winning share of just one slice.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
